eportal_cooling_permits.description: IMDC VA1 CHILLER ADDITON

power.note: VADEQ air permit 74112 covers this site with 370.2 MW of permitted backup generator capacity across 8 building(s). This building's 8% floor-area share x ICPRB Equation 6-3 (capacity x 0.5 redundancy x 0.8 utilization) = 12.0 MW effective IT load. Floor area is used only to apportion a measured site total, not to generate it -- the 8,818 sqft/MW density bridge is not used for this building.

operator_cross_check.note: interconnection.fyi lists 100-250 MW across IRON MOUNTAIN's Prince William / Manassas portfolio. The floor-area-derived estimate falls outside that span; the operator figure is portfolio-wide rather than building-specific, so it is reported as a flag rather than used to widen the range.

scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.3-1.55, standard vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.004 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

power.note: 182,032 sqft -> 18.0 MW effective IT load (implied 10,137 sqft/MW). The 90% interval (x/1.51) is the measured residual of that fit -- the quantified cost of knowing only floor area.

WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.004 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

power.note: VADEQ air permit 74161 covers this site with 362.1 MW of permitted backup generator capacity across 6 building(s). This building's 23% floor-area share x ICPRB Equation 6-3 (capacity x 0.5 redundancy x 0.8 utilization) = 33.7 MW effective IT load. Floor area is used only to apportion a measured site total, not to generate it -- the 8,818 sqft/MW density bridge is not used for this building.

operator_cross_check.note: interconnection.fyi lists 250-400 MW across QTS's Prince William / Manassas portfolio. The floor-area-derived estimate falls outside that span; the operator figure is portfolio-wide rather than building-specific, so it is reported as a flag rather than used to widen the range.

scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

power.note: VADEQ air permit 74262 covers this site with 789.2 MW of permitted backup generator capacity across 4 building(s). scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

Floor area is used only to apportion a measured site total, not to generate it -- the 8,818 sqft/MW density bridge is not used for this building.

operator_cross_check.note: interconnection.fyi lists 50-250 MW across AMAZON's Prince William / Manassas portfolio. The floor-area-derived estimate falls outside that span; the operator figure is portfolio-wide rather than building-specific, so it is reported as a flag rather than used to widen the range.

scope1_onsite_cooling.narrowed_by: AMAZON: Amazon/AWS reports deploying closed-loop, direct-to-chip cold-plate cooling that adds no evaporative water on new AI infrastructure, and a 42% year-over-year water reduction in its Northern Virginia region (2025 sustainability reporting). Global fleet WUE 0.12 L/kWh.
scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-309 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

market_based.caveat: Contractual, not physical. Annual REC/PPA matching does not change which plant served this building at 3pm in August, and the water consumed there was consumed there. Reported because the GHG Protocol requires dual reporting and operators quote this figure; the location-based value above is the one that corresponds to water actually leaving a Virginia basin.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.08-1.2, AWS 2025 global average PUE 1.14 (1.15 in 2024)) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.002 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

scope1_onsite_cooling.narrowed_by: AMAZON: Amazon/AWS reports deploying closed-loop, direct-to-chip cold-plate cooling that adds no evaporative water on new AI infrastructure, and a 42% year-over-year water reduction in its Northern Virginia region (2025 sustainability reporting). scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.08-1.2, AWS 2025 global average PUE 1.14 (1.15 in 2024)) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.020 MGD) sits in the normal measured band for Virginia data centers (JLARC 2024).

Power is INFERRED, not observed: fitted GFA->MW model (n=14 independent permit sites, leak-free site-level fit, winner by LOO-CV: ridge_operator; slope 1.00, LOO residual x/1.28; no operator calibration -- generic curve). scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.007 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

Power is INFERRED, not observed: fitted GFA->MW model (n=14 independent permit sites, leak-free site-level fit, winner by LOO-CV: ridge_operator; slope 1.00, LOO residual x/1.28; no operator calibration -- generic curve). scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.002 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.015 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.035 MGD) sits in the normal measured band for Virginia data centers (JLARC 2024).

power.note: 198,500 sqft -> 22.8 MW effective IT load (implied 8,722 sqft/MW). Power is INFERRED, not observed: fitted GFA->MW model (n=14 independent permit sites, leak-free site-level fit, winner by LOO-CV: ridge_operator; slope 1.00, LOO residual x/1.28; no operator calibration -- generic curve). scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

operator_cross_check.note: interconnection.fyi lists 50-250 MW across AMAZON's Prince William / Manassas portfolio. The floor-area-derived estimate falls inside that span.

power.hv_plausibility: Nearest in-service >=230kV HIFLD line is 0.3 mi away, consistent with this load.

scope1_onsite_cooling.narrowed_by: AMAZON: Amazon/AWS reports deploying closed-loop, direct-to-chip cold-plate cooling that adds no evaporative water on new AI infrastructure, and a 42% year-over-year water reduction in its Northern Virginia region (2025 sustainability reporting). Global fleet WUE 0.12 L/kWh.
scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-309 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

market_based.caveat: Contractual, not physical. Annual REC/PPA matching does not change which plant served this building at 3pm in August, and the water consumed there was consumed there. Reported because the GHG Protocol requires dual reporting and operators quote this figure; the location-based value above is the one that corresponds to water actually leaving a Virginia basin.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.08-1.2, AWS 2025 global average PUE 1.14 (1.15 in 2024)) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.007 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

marginal_based.basis: PJM marginal-fuel mix (2022): combined-cycle gas 61.7% of marginal hours, peaking gas 17.2%, coal 10.0%, wind 11.1%; nuclear ~never marginal. A new load turns on gas, not the nuclear baseload, so this reallocates consumption off the York basin (North Anna) and onto the James (gas fleet).

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 226 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from the USGS 2008-2020 thermoelectric reanalysis (Galanter et al. 2023), pooled 2018-2020, rather than national medians -- nuclear is 391 gal/MWh here (North Anna evaporates ~737 from its cooling lake while Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing), against a national median of 700.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.
